chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Khalid al-Maraghi reported to me, saying: Abul Qasim al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Ja‘far ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Masih ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ali ibn Abu Umrah al-Khurasani narrated to me, from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Ishaq al-Sabiee, who said:

We called upon Masrooq ibn al-Ajda and found a guest with him who we did not know. They were having their meal together. Then the guest said: “I was with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, at Hunayn.” When he said that, we knew that he had been a companion of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace.

He said: Then Safiyyah, daughter of Huyayy ibn Akhtab, came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, and said: “O Messenger of Allah, I am not like any one of your wives—my father, brother, and uncle were killed. If something were to happen to you, to whom would I turn?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said to her: “To this one,” and he pointed to Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him.

He said: “Shall I not relate to you what al-Harith al-A‘war narrated to me?” We said: “Please do.” He said: “I called upon Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, and he said: ‘What brings you here, O A‘war?’ I replied: ‘Your love, O Commander of the Faithful.’ He asked: ‘By Allah?’ I said: ‘By Allah.’ He confirmed with me three times. Then he said:

Verily, there is no servant of Allah whose heart He has tested for faith except that he finds our love upon his heart, and so he loves us. And there is no servant of Allah upon whom Allah has shown His displeasure except that he finds our hatred upon his heart, and so he hates us. So, the one who loves us awaits the mercy, and the gates of mercy have been opened for him. And the one who hates us stands upon the edge of a crumbling bank, which has tumbled down with him into the fire of Hell. Bounteous is the mercy for those who receive it, and perdition is the abode of those destined for the Fire.

key_terms.امتحان القلب: Testing of the heart for faith, a divine trial of sincerity
key_terms.شفا جرف هار: The edge of a crumbling bank, a Qur’anic metaphor (9:109) for an unstable foundation leading to ruin
key_terms.صفيّة بنت حُيي: Safiyyah bint Huyayy, wife of the Prophet (SAW), of Jewish origin
key_terms.مودّة: Loving affection (mawaddah), especially for the Prophet’s family as referenced in Quran 42:23

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali teach about love and hatred for the Ahl al-Bayt as a sign of faith?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) teaches that love and hatred for the Ahl al-Bayt are divinely placed in hearts as a test of faith. Through a chain of narrators, including Abu Ishaq al-Sabiee and al-Harith al-A‘war, the hadith also preserves the Prophet’s designation of Ali (AS) as guardian for Safiyyah bint Huyayy, his wife who had lost her father, brother, and uncle. Ali (AS) confirms three times al-Harith’s claim of love, then declares that those whose hearts Allah has tested for faith find love for the Ahl al-Bayt naturally, while those under divine displeasure harbor hatred. Lovers of the Ahl al-Bayt await mercy with its gates open, while haters stand upon a crumbling precipice over Hellfire—echoing Quran 9:109.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 2. He said: Abul Hasan ‘Ali ibn Khalid al-Maraghi reported to me from Abul Qasim al-Hasan ibn ‘Ali al-Kufi, who reported from Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan, who reported from his father, who reported from Masih ibn Muhammad, who reported from Abu ‘Ali ibn Abu Umrah al-Khurasani, from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim from Abu Ishaq al-Sabiee’, who said:

We called upon Masrooq ibn al-Ajda and found a guest who we did not know. They were having their meals; and then the guest observed that he was with the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, at Hunayn. Just as he said that, we knew he was a companion of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny.

He said: Then Safiyyah, daughter of Hay ibn Akhtab (one of the wives of the Prophet) came to the Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, and said: "O messenger of Allah, I am not like your other wives who have father, brother and uncle. If anything were to happen to you, to who do you entrust me?" The Prophet, peace be upon him and his progeny, pointing at ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him said: "To him."

Then he said: "May I not relate to you what al-Harith ibn al-A’awar narrated to us?" We said: "Please do." He said: I called upon ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him and his progeny, and he asked: "O A’awar, what brings you here?" A’awar says he replied: "O Amirul Mu’mineen, your love has brought us." He asked: "Really?" I said: "Yes, Allah is my witness." He confirmed with me three times. Then he said:

"There is no slave of Allah who He has tested for piety, except that He finds our love in his heart; such a person indeed loves us. And there is no slave of Allah upon whom Allah has shown His displeasure, except that He finds our hatred in his heart, and such a person indeed hates us. So, our friends always expect the divine mercy, and the gates of mercy are open for them. And our enemies are upon the edge of crumbling bank that will tumble down with them in to the fire of hell. Bounteous is the mercy for the people who earn it, and perdition is for the people of hell fire."
